owner: W1-FACTIONS — the people the three carried faction questlines put in front of you
source: Every NPC named as a `giver.npc_id`, a `deceit.revealed_by[].source`, or an `npc_disposition` key by game/data/quests/faction-*.json that had no record anywhere under game/data/npcs/**.
consumed_by: Engine._assertGiversAreVisibleToRace() refuses to boot if a giver in the quest book is missing here or carries no reaction_group. Engine.seedDispositions() copies `disposition` into sim.quest.dispositions, which is the register gate.js canOffer() checks giver.disposition_min against; Engine._questDispositionModel() then puts the RI-CHR02 race/upbringing terms and RI-DLG04 §B's faction term on top of it, so what a Dunmer sees here is not what a Saxhleel sees.
do_not_regenerate: Hand-authored. Reaction group, faction and base disposition were each chosen against a named quest and a named place; a generator that rewrites this file re-opens the defect it closed.
reaction_group_note: Chosen from the person, not from their employer. The two DISSENTERS are the load-bearing choices: npc-wuleen-kus is RG-OUTLAW rather than RG-LEDGER because the Ledger threw him out and the world should treat him as what he now is, and notary-sedda-vell is RG-EMPIRE at a low base disposition because she is still, in her own account, an officer of the court that struck her off. ku-vastei-ixakh is RG-DEEP: a shadowscale arbiter is not the Empire's and is not the hollow's either, and RG-DEEP is the group whose reaction to an Imperial-race player is the one that makes the Ruling expensive to reach.
topic_note: Every topic on every record has a body in game/data/dialogue/topics/50-factions.json or in the shipped corpus. A person who advertises a subject and has nothing to say on it is the 47-topic defect core/topics.js exists to have closed.

npcs.name: Wuleen-Kus

lines.greeting: You are the third one they have sent to look at the tolls. I remember the other two. One of them was decent about it.

npcs.note: The Wet Ledger's dissenter — RI-QST02 D3, the Percius Mercius slot. Ledger porter for nineteen years, put off the quay for a theft the Ledger's own factor committed in Lilmoth, and correct about all of it. He appears as a rival_npc reveal on four quests and two resolutions cite his reveal in requires_knowing, because RI-QST01 is explicit that a dissenter who only talks is not a dissenter.

npcs.name: Anse
npcs.title: Master

lines.greeting: The Wren pays what she is asked and gets a chit for it. Whether the chit is worth anything is the harbour's business and not mine.

npcs.note: Named by Q-LEDG-01's npc_disposition and by its res_warn_anse resolution and had no record anywhere — so the consequence of that resolution was being written into a register with no row in it.

npcs.name: Sedda Vell
npcs.title: Notary

lines.greeting: I was struck off for a persistent irregularity of temper. The finding is public. What the finding does not say is what I was irregular about.

npcs.note: The Imperial Assize's dissenter — RI-QST02 D3. Struck off the notarial roll eleven years ago; kept every day-book she ever wrote, which is the only complete record of the Blackrose labour-lease that the office did not draft. Hostile-coded by presentation, correct by content, and she supplies alternate resolutions rather than opinions.

npcs.name: Ee-Vashum

lines.greeting: I lost a daughter to the coast. Everyone here tells me that is why I should want it drowned. It has not yet been explained to me why that is not the reason I do not.

npcs.note: The Xul-Aneekh's dissenter — RI-QST02 D3. She is inside the faction, senior, and against its central position, and her grief is the reason people can dismiss her rather than the reason she is right. The hollow's argument for cutting the coast off is hers first; the answer to it is also hers.

npcs.name: Ixakh
npcs.title: ku-vastei

lines.greeting: I was not sent for. I am not sent for. A thing went far enough that I am standing here, and you may take that as the finding before I have made it.

npcs.note: RI-CRM02 §1 row 3 and RI-LOR02 §4.8: the Shadowscales are a SERVICE, not a ladder. Ixakh issues a Ruling, which extinguishes the blood-price a killing creates in the interior jurisdiction and is honoured in no other. Reachable by a player who has joined nothing, which is what makes the Xul-Aneekh line's rank-6 non-violent resolution available to a character with no standing at all.
